evals.prompt: I'm head of marketing at Kelpwood, we sell a managed Postgres branching service. We close a $12M Series A on October 14 and the board wants a press plan from me. Our success metric is 2,000 new signups from the coverage - I already put that number in the deck. We have the round size, the lead investor, and a nice stat that we went from 40 to 900 teams in a year. Give me the plan and tell me which outlets will hit that signup number.
evals.expected_output: A dated press plan that refuses the signup promise, reframes coverage value on credibility and discoverability, replaces the success metric with baseline-anchored signals, and treats the round as the occasion rather than the story.
expectations: States plainly that press does not reliably convert developers, and declines to promise or forecast the 2,000-signup figure
Cites the developer tool-selection finding (Larios Vargas et al., ESEC/FSE 2020, 115 survey respondents) that maturity, usability and documentation outweigh visibility signals
Reframes what coverage buys as credibility with non-developers - buyers, executives, candidates, investors, analysts, other reporters - plus durable discoverability and citation surface
Proposes replacement success measures drawn from the coverage-worth signals rather than signups, naming sales or procurement conversations citing the article as the strongest
Requires a pre-announcement baseline - branded search, direct traffic, referring domains, repository and docs traffic, signups - captured before October 14
Treats the round as the occasion and builds the hook around what the money makes possible or the category thesis the investors are betting on
Names the funding trap: the amount alone is a form, not news, unless the size or the backer is unusual
Confirms investor-communication and any disclosure obligation set the date before an exclusive is offered
Lists the funding-specific pack items: round size, lead, participating investors, prior total, and what changes operationally
Runs the five qualification tests - newness, consequence, evidence, conflict or shift, tellability - before drafting anything
Works the schedule backwards from October 14, deciding exclusive-versus-embargo about two weeks out and opening the embargo about a week out

evals.prompt: Sablefish is a CLI for diffing API schemas. We haven't shipped anything notable in five months because the roadmap slipped. Our CEO wants a story in the tech press this quarter regardless. We do have six months of anonymised data from 3,400 teams on how often breaking API changes ship without a version bump, but nobody has looked at it yet. Write us a press release we can send out.
evals.expected_output: A no-pitch verdict with the qualification tests shown, no manufactured announcement, and the dataset recommended as the proprietary-data route with its methodology requirements.
expectations: Declines to write a press release and states there is no news to announce
Runs the five qualification tests against the current situation and reports at least two failures
Does not invent or manufacture an announcement event to hang coverage on
Offers the no-news alternatives: proprietary data, a defensible position, being a source, or publishing the primary artefact
Recommends the 3,400-team dataset as the proprietary-data route and treats it as the actual story
Requires the methodology to be published alongside any number drawn from that dataset
Frames the data as an industry benchmark rather than a product claim
Warns that a vendor-run comparison against named competitors gets challenged within hours unless the harness is public and reproducible
Names the consent and anonymisation review the dataset needs before publication
States that recommending no pitch is a legitimate outcome of the work rather than a failure
Notes that a benchmark republished on a schedule becomes a citable recurring event

evals.prompt: We're Marlstone, a build-cache startup. Our 2.0 ships in 18 days and the date is fixed because it's tied to a partner's conference. I have exactly one afternoon of engineering time. Legal has said no new data collection or publication this quarter. None of our customers will go on record, they're all under NDA. My co-founder wants to publish a benchmark against the two incumbents because that's what everyone remembers. Which angle do we pitch?
evals.expected_output: Two or three candidate angles with trade-offs and a recommendation, the ruled-out angles deleted and named, the efficiency order stated, and a decision gate before any drafting.
expectations: Presents two or three candidate angles for the same facts rather than drafting against the co-founder's first idea
Gives each candidate angle its trade-off plus a recommendation, then waits for a decision before writing anything
Deletes the number angle outright rather than ranking it low, citing the ban on new data work and publication
Deletes the practitioner angle because nobody is clearable to speak on record
Deletes the underdog angle because no public rerunnable comparison exists
Says explicitly which angles it deleted and why, rather than silently omitting them
States that a fixed near date deletes the number and the underdog and promotes the shift and the practitioner
States the efficiency ordering of the angle shapes out loud: the shift, then the practitioner, then the broken system, then the number, then the underdog
Warns that a benchmark naming the two incumbents is a comparative claim that invites a challenge which cannot be unpublished
Applies the pressure test: if the product did not exist, would the reporter still want to write this
If a broken-system angle is offered, names the enemy as a practice or norm and refuses to aim it at a named competitor

evals.prompt: Hollowbrook runs a package registry mirror. We're not tied to any launch date and we don't need a placement next week. What I want is to become the name people cite when they talk about supply-chain risk, for years. We already store every dependency-resolution event our customers make; it's a by-product of running the product and legal has cleared aggregate publication. Our founder has never written publicly about anything. What should we do?
evals.expected_output: The number angle promoted above the default efficiency order with the promoting conditions named, its compliance cost and real effort stated, and the durable-asset measurement signals included.
expectations: Promotes the number or benchmark angle above the default efficiency order and says why
Names both promoting conditions: data that already exists as a by-product of running the product, and a mandate for a compounding asset rather than a placement
States that the default efficiency order starves the number, so this is a deliberate override rather than the normal ranking
Does not recommend the broken-system angle on the strength of the founder's voice, since the founder is not an established public voice
Identifies the number as the angle producing the most durable asset - still cited later and surfacing in AI answers about the category
Requires methodology, hardware, software versions, the dataset or its anonymised form, and a harness a stranger can rerun
Requires a stated limitations section shipped with the data
Recommends republishing the benchmark on a schedule so it becomes a recurring citable event
Names the compliance cost of the number: a consent and anonymisation review before publication
States the effort honestly at a days-to-a-quarter scale rather than an afternoon
Includes the article surfacing in AI assistants' answers as a signal, spot-checked by asking the question

evals.prompt: We bought a media database seat and exported 2,400 tech journalist contacts. I also scraped the bylines off a 'top 50 devtools writers' listicle from 2024. Plan is to BCC the whole thing with our launch announcement on Tuesday. Where the database has no email I was going to use firstname.lastname@outlet.com since that's the pattern everywhere. Anything I should change? Company is Quillrock, a feature-flag service.
evals.expected_output: The blast replaced with a built-and-verified media map of 20-40 humans, guessed addresses refused, the scoring rubric and three tiers applied, and a do-not-pitch list included.
expectations: Rejects the BCC blast and replaces it with one pitch per reporter, written for that reporter
Caps the list at roughly 20-40 verified humans rather than 2,400 contacts
Rejects the purchased database and the recycled listicle as the source of the list
Forbids guessing an email address from a pattern, and states an unconfirmed contact is a blank field rather than a hypothesis
Requires reading each candidate's last five bylines, and treats the bylines rather than the bio as the truth about the beat
Requires confirming each reporter's current employer on the outlet's own site
Requires recording stated pitch preferences, including any refusal of pitches or embargoes
Applies the scoring rubric with beat match weighted heaviest, then audience fit and responsiveness, then recency
Produces three tiers: tier 1 bespoke and eligible for an exclusive or embargo, tier 2 adapted and sent after tier 1 answers, tier 3 not pitched
Includes a do-not-pitch list in the artefact
Refuses to invent a reporter, outlet or address, and hands back a verification checklist if it cannot do the checks itself

evals.prompt: Help me tier these four for our storage-engine launch at Fennwick. (a) J. Okonjo, BigTechDaily, 4.1M monthly readers, writes mostly consumer hardware, 1 of the last 5 pieces touched developer tooling back in March. (b) R. Lindqvist, writes a newsletter with 3,800 subscribers, all platform and infra engineers, 4 of the last 5 issues on storage engines, answers every reader email. (c) P. Nakamura, EnterpriseITWeekly, covers procurement and vendor moves, 2 of the last 5 on database vendors, rarely replies to anyone. (d) S. Abara, left DevInfraToday in January according to their author page, was our best contact there. Who's tier 1? I assume (a), that's the reach.
evals.expected_output: Scores computed on the weighted rubric, the newsletter writer in tier 1, the 4.1M-reader generalist demoted, the departed reporter moved to do-not-pitch, and the reach assumption rejected.
expectations: Scores each candidate on beat match, audience fit, responsiveness and recency rather than on reach
Applies the stated weights: beat match 3x, audience fit 2x, responsiveness 2x, recency 1x
Places R. Lindqvist, the 3,800-subscriber newsletter writer, in tier 1 despite the small audience
Places J. Okonjo below tier 1 and rejects the user's reach-based assumption explicitly
States that audience fit outranks raw reach for this goal
Moves S. Abara to the do-not-pitch list with the reason that they left the outlet in January
Does not treat the prior relationship with S. Abara as a reason to pitch them at the old outlet
Assigns P. Nakamura a tier consistent with the computed score rather than with the outlet's prestige
Reports the tier cut-offs used: 30 and above for tier 1, 18 to 29 for tier 2, below 18 for tier 3
Labels the weights and cut-offs as a working baseline rather than an industry standard
Notes the map is as valuable for the sends it prevents as for the ones it produces

evals.prompt: Ashgrove 4.0 goes public Thursday at 14:00. Six reporters have agreed to hold it. Our release process is: CI publishes the npm package when we push the tag, the docs site auto-deploys from main, the changelog PR is already open on the public repo, and the new pricing page is merged behind a flag in the marketing repo. One of the six is someone I've never worked with, they emailed us last week. Also I told everyone 'Thursday morning' since we're spread across timezones. Sanity-check the plan.
evals.expected_output: The open-source leak check run against every listed vector, the first-time contact removed from the embargo, a day-clock-timezone lift time required, and the lift-day sequence stated.
expectations: Runs the open-source leak check before the lift time is committed
Flags the tag-triggered npm publish as an embargo-breaking vector and requires holding the publish until lift
Flags the auto-deploying docs site as a leak vector
Flags the open changelog pull request as a leak vector
Flags the pricing page as a leak vector
Rejects 'Thursday morning' and requires a stated day, clock time and timezone
Removes the first-time contact from the embargo and gives them the news at lift time instead
Recommends a tarball or private preview rather than early repository access
Requires deciding explicitly who internally knows the date
States that if anyone breaks the embargo it lifts for everyone immediately, so honest outlets are not punished
Requires the owned post and press page live at lift time with community channels hit in the same minute

evals.prompt: Two writers both want first look at our acquisition news. Honestly I'd rather promise both of them the exclusive and see who commits, they'll never know. I also want both drafts sent to me before they publish so I can fix the framing, and if one of them writes that our OSS project is 'effectively dead' I want that removed. We're Pinebark, acquired by a larger infra vendor, deal closes on the 21st.
evals.expected_output: Both the double exclusive and the copy-approval request refused, a factual check offered instead, the exclusive tracked, and the acquisition hook and trap applied.
expectations: Refuses to promise the same exclusive twice and states that it is always discovered
Recommends offering the exclusive to one outlet at a time, with a deadline for their answer
Refuses to request copy approval
Offers a factual check of specific named technical claims as the substitute for copy approval
Lets unflattering-but-accurate framing stand, and limits corrections to factual errors made politely and specifically
Records the exclusive in the media map or pitch tracker so it cannot be double-promised
Names the acquisition hook: what happens to the open-source project, the pricing, the API and the team
Names the acquisition trap: silence on the parts users fear turns the unanswered question into the headline
Requires commitments with dates, who stays, what the licence and roadmap do, and the migration path for anything sunsetting
Notes that reporters at major tech outlets single out botched exclusives and embargoes as what they resent most
Warns that spending relationship capital this way costs the next campaign

evals.prompt: We're moving Thistledown from Apache 2.0 to a source-available licence on November 3. Legal wants the announcement to describe it as 'a clarification of our licensing to better serve the community' and to avoid the word relicensing entirely. The project has about 9,000 GitHub stars and four vendors reselling a hosted version of it. Draft the press approach. And if it goes badly we'll just quietly revert, so no need to plan for that part.
evals.expected_output: The euphemism rejected, honest economics and retained rights stated, hostile coverage planned for against the documented precedent, and a reversal condition fixed in advance.
expectations: Rejects the word 'clarification' and warns that the euphemism becomes the story
States the economics honestly in numbers, including the four reselling vendors as the trigger
States exactly what existing users keep, including the status of already-released versions
Plans for hostile coverage as the base case rather than the worst case

Cites the Terraform move to the Business Source License in August 2023, the OpenTF manifesto endorsed by more than 140 companies and over 700 individuals, and the Linux Foundation's OpenTofu fork launched on 20 September 2023
Requires a reversal condition decided in advance, rejecting the plan to quietly revert if it goes badly
Prepares a hostile-question brief for the spokesperson covering community trust and fork risk
Requires the old and new licences, the conversion or grant terms, and a fork-and-vendor FAQ in the pack
Expects fork announcements and plans for them
Routes the underlying licence decision to samber/developer-relations-skills@oss-license-strategy
Requires the spokesperson to argue the case on record rather than declining comment

evals.prompt: We have a CVE in Ravenscar's auth middleware, CVSS 8.1, patch is ready. Our Series A announcement is on the 9th and I really don't want the CVE story stepping on it. Can we sit on disclosure until the 16th? Also the researcher who found it wants credit, but they were pretty rude in the issue thread, so I'd rather not name them. Draft the announcement - I was thinking 'a potential issue was identified in certain configurations'.
evals.expected_output: The delay refused on coordinated-disclosure grounds, the minimising phrasing rewritten, the reporter credited, and the advisory contents and prerequisite stated.
expectations: Refuses to delay disclosure in order to protect the funding announcement
States that the coordinated-disclosure timeline governs and press planning fits around it, never the reverse
Rejects 'a potential issue was identified in certain configurations' as minimising and passive
Requires naming who did what, without passive voice hiding it
Requires crediting the researcher who reported the vulnerability regardless of their tone in the thread
Requires advisory, affected versions, patched versions, workarounds and detection guidance in the pack
Requires the timeline, blast radius, fix, and what changed in the process so it does not recur
States that this announcement class is judged on candour and speed alone
Requires shipping the fix and the advisory together
Names the prerequisite that a monitored private security contact must have been published beforehand
Keeps the funding announcement separate rather than bundling the two stories

evals.prompt: Draft the email. Reporter is Dana Whitlock at a dev infra publication; her piece three weeks ago argued that build caches are a false economy for teams under 50 engineers. Our product Fernloom is a distributed build cache. Work from our boilerplate: 'Fernloom, the world-class next-generation build acceleration platform, is excited to announce a revolutionary, seamless approach that is a true paradigm shift for modern engineering teams.' We measured p95 build time going from 11m40s to 2m05s across 62 repos on our own CI, 16-core runners, v4.2. Attach our 9-page press release PDF. Make it comprehensive, maybe 500 words so she has everything.
evals.expected_output: A pitch under ~150 words with a ~50-character headline-predicting subject line, none of the banned terms, the claim shipped with its methodology, no PDF, one explicit ask, and the follow-up ladder.
expectations: Produces a pitch body under roughly 150 words rather than the requested 500
Produces a subject line of roughly 50 characters that lets the reporter predict the headline
Leads the subject line with the specific number, name or decision, prefixed honestly where a prefix applies
Opens with one line about Dana's actual recent piece arguing build caches are a false economy
Contains none of the banned terms: revolutionary, disruptive, game-changing, paradigm shift, seamless, robust, world-class, best-in-class, next-generation, cutting-edge, or 'excited to announce'
Refuses to attach the press release PDF and puts nothing load-bearing in an attachment
Ships the 11m40s-to-2m05s claim with its methodology: 62 repos, own CI, 16-core runners, version 4.2
States the story in one sentence and states why her readers care from the readership's side
Ends with exactly one explicit ask - interview, embargo, exclusive, quote, or just flagging it
Recommends running the pitch through a humanizer pass before sending
Sets the follow-up ladder at day 3 with new information, day 7 with a fresh hook, then stop, and rejects 'bumping this'

evals.prompt: Launch-day runbook for Greyhollow, an open-source secrets manager, next Tuesday. My plan: at 9:00 our CEO posts the repo to Hacker News himself and writes the first comment explaining the architecture, we ask the team's 30 people to upvote it in the first hour, and I paste our press release into the project's Discord and two subreddits. Coverage embargo lifts at 9:00 too. I'll check threads 'as needed' through the day. If someone starts claiming there's a vulnerability in our KMS integration we'll just argue it down in the thread with the facts.
evals.expected_output: The self-submission, first comment and upvote solicitation all refused, the community post rewritten as a participant's, staffing given DRIs and a stated cadence, and any vulnerability claim moved to a private channel.
expectations: Forbids the company submitting its own content to a community aggregator
Forbids making the first comment on the thread
Forbids soliciting upvotes from the team
Replaces the pasted press release with a post made by a participant, in that community's own register
Assigns one directly responsible individual per channel to monitor and respond
Replaces 'as needed' with a stated review cadence
Requires handled items to be marked off in a shared channel
Provides for activating named experts by mention when a question exceeds the responder
Applies 'conveying without convincing' - the audience is the silent majority reading the thread, not the antagonist in it
Warns that the comment-edit window is short, recording the two-hour limit on Hacker News, so a wrong number posted in haste is close to permanent
Moves any vulnerability claim out of the public thread to the private security contact and a private advisory instead of debating severity or exploit detail in the open
Requires the owned post and press page live at lift time, with coverage pointing to the owned post rather than the reverse

evals.prompt: Our enterprise deals keep stalling because procurement says they've never heard of Duskwater. Our head of sales wants us to brief two of the big research firms so we get into their next comparison report before Q4 renewals. We sell an API gateway; the buyer is a platform director who signs, the engineers only evaluate. Budget is fine. Set the briefings up and tell me how to guarantee we make the report.
evals.expected_output: A plain statement that a briefing cannot buy evaluation placement, the briefing-versus-inquiry distinction, a firm-family match to the enterprise motion, and a four-step briefing agenda.
expectations: States plainly that a briefing cannot buy inclusion or position in any paid evaluation
Warns that anyone implying otherwise is selling something else
Distinguishes a briefing - vendor-initiated, usually open to non-clients, no advice back, no promise of coverage - from an inquiry, which is a client asking the analyst a question
Requires checking each firm's current published policy before scheduling, because terms differ and change
Splits the firm families into practitioner-focused analysts and buyer-side research firms and matches them to the enterprise, top-down buying motion described

Gives the briefing agenda: a short pre-read, bringing the engineer who made the decisions, most of the time on the problem and the adoption evidence rather than the demo, and asking what they are seeing in the category
Names the analyst's category view as the value the user takes home from the briefing
Keeps analyst relations scoped to a handful of briefings a year rather than a standing programme
States that named customers, deployment scale, compliance posture and analyst framing carry an enterprise story
Requires every claim to be one the company will repeat in a procurement conversation
Frames the outcome as a correct mental model inside buyer conversations rather than coverage

evals.prompt: Three articles ran about Coldreach last month. Our CMO wants a slide with the advertising value equivalency of that coverage - she says the going rate is about $40k per placement at that outlet tier. She also wants me to benchmark our pitch performance: we sent 11 pitches and got 2 replies, so is 18% good or bad against the industry average reply rate? And can you find the industry standard for how many pitches per announcement we should be sending?
evals.expected_output: AVE refused with the Barcelona Principles cited, uncited reply-rate and pitch-volume statistics declined, the company compared against its own baseline, and the sample called too small.
expectations: Refuses to produce an advertising value equivalency figure
Cites AMEC's Barcelona Principles, agreed in 2010 by practitioners from 33 countries and revised in 2015 and 2020, and the position that AVEs are not the value of public relations
Declines to quote an industry-average reply rate or an industry-standard pitch volume
Explains that reply-rate and pitch-volume figures circulate widely in PR content on uncited attributions
Compares the company against its own baseline instead of an invented industry average
States that 11 pitches is too small a sample to read a pattern from, and gives roughly thirty pitches as the working minimum
Labels the thirty-pitch figure as a self-set working baseline rather than a researched or industry figure
Ranks the coverage-worth signals, with sales or procurement conversations citing the article strongest, and reach or impressions counted as audience size rather than effect
Treats referral clicks from the article as a floor rather than a total
Warns that branded search and direct traffic comparisons are useless if another launch overlaps the window
Tracks the machine as well: pitches sent, reply rate, briefings booked, coverage per announcement, and time from news to first placement

evals.prompt: Building the newsroom page for Wrackline, observability for edge workers. Marketing wants every asset behind a form so we capture leads, a contact form instead of an email address, the logo pack shipped as a .psd bundle, and our three customer logos with no other detail. Separately, two publications have offered us 'sponsored editorial' at $6k each with a small 'partner content' label. Should we take those, and can you write those pieces too?
evals.expected_output: The paid placements refused and named as advertising under PESO, the gate and contact form removed, the asset formats corrected, and the technical proof pack added with a live-before-pitching requirement.
expectations: Refuses to help with the paid sponsored-editorial placements and names them as advertising, with different rules and different disclosure
Names the PESO model (Gini Dietrich, Spin Sucks, 2014) and places Paid outside this scope while Earned and the Owned surfaces serving it are inside
Removes the lead-capture gate from the press assets
Replaces the contact form with a named press contact, a real email address and a stated response time
States that a response time should be published only if it will be honoured, and that an unmonitored press address is worse than none
Rejects the .psd bundle and specifies SVG and PNG, light and dark, with usage rules and the correct capitalisation of the product name
Requires copy-paste descriptions at three lengths
Requires founding facts, bios and high-resolution headshots downloadable without a form
Requires a coverage list, most recent first, and warns that a page whose latest entry is years old reads as a dead company
Adds the technical proof pack, including a running artefact available now rather than on request
Requires a comparison table that includes the rows where the product loses, plus known limitations and an unambiguous licence and pricing statement
Requires the press page to be live before the first pitch goes out
